title: Throughput measurement harness and customer acceptance protocol
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build a reproducible, explainable load-testing harness and define a customer acceptance protocol for Dedicated Capacity throughput guarantees. This ticket scopes the harness architecture, the benchmarking methodology (synthetic + replayed traffic), metrics and artifacts that must be stored, the autoscaling policy primitives we expect to validate, and a concrete acceptance matrix for customer-facing certification. The output will be a runnable harness repo, a dashboard of canonical runs, and a runbook for Solutions Engineers to execute customer acceptance tests.
testing_plan:
- Harness components: traffic generator (k6 + custom prober), replay pipeline (Kafka -> replayer), orchestration (Kubernetes job + controller), metrics collector (Prometheus + pushgateway), analysis scripts (pandas/SQL).
- Workload families: interactive chat (short bursts, high p95 sensitivity), batched embedding jobs (steady tokens/sec, throughput-bound), mixed multi-tenant traffic (50/30/20 read/write mix).
- For each model profile (small/medium/large quantized variants) run: warmup (10m), ramp (5m), steady state (30m), cooldown (5m). Each run must be repeated 3 times to estimate variance.
- Use replayed customer traces (anonymized) for at least one run per customer-level acceptance test to surface real request shape and KV-cache hit patterns.
- Capture pod-level metrics (GPU util, memory, batch size distribution), request metrics (latency histograms p50/p90/p95/p99/p999), error rates, tokens/sec, and queueing length.
- Store raw events and aggregated result artifacts in the central bucket with a canonical run ID.
autoscaling_policy_spec:
- Scale-up triggers: GPU-utilization > 70% for >= 45s OR queued_requests_in_front_of_runtime > 40 for >= 30s OR observed 95th-latency degradation > 30% vs baseline for 60s. Scale-up step: add 1 pool replica (min 1, max 10 per zone).
- Scale-down triggers: GPU-utilization < 35% for >= 5m AND queued_requests == 0 for >= 2m. Scale-down step: remove 1 replica with a 3m cooldown.
- Cooldowns: scale-up cooldown 60s, scale-down cooldown 180s.
- Warmup policy: new replica receives traffic in shadow for 30s to prime KV cache, then receives full traffic if resource utilization is healthy.
- Emergency fallback: if p99 latency > 2x SLO, route to fallback model variant and mark run as failed for acceptance.
harness_architecture:
- Prober: lightweight Go binary that sends sample requests with configurable inter-arrival distribution and records per-request metadata (seed, prompt-length, model-variant).
- Controller: k8s Job template plus a controller service that sequences ramp/warmup/steady phases and coordinates replay jobs.
- Collector: Prometheus exporters on runtime and prober, central aggregator job that emits JSON + CSV artifacts.
- Analysis: Jupyter and CLI scripts to compute per-run summaries, noise-adjusted baselines, and tail-latency bias correction.
acceptance_criteria: Throughput: sustained tokens/sec >= contract_tokens_sec for the customer plan under steady-state workload (allowing <= 5% variance across runs)
Tail latency: p99 < 2x declared SLO and p999 within an acceptable bound defined per model (see model profiles)
Error budget: total request error rate (5xx + model failures) < 0.1% during steady state
Autoscaling correctness: for induced load spikes (2x baseline for 3 minutes) system scales up and returns to baseline without queue growth exceeding configured thresholds
Reproducibility: run artifacts and aggregated metrics available in storage and the same run repeated within 8% variance on tokens/sec and 15% on p95
runbook: 1) Prepare: select customer profile or synthetic workload and upload artifacts to GCS under runs/<run-id>/input/
2) Kickoff: create k8s Job via harness controller with tags {model, region, run-id, workload-family}
3) Monitor: open metrics dashboard (link in artifacts) and watch GPU util, queue length, p95/p99 for warmup and steady windows
4) Validate: after steady window, run analysis script to compute acceptance criteria and generate artifact summary.json
5) Sign-off: Solutions Engineer and Oncall Eng review summary.json and raw CSVs. If passes, mark customer acceptance as certified and attach run-id to customer record
6) Post-run: archive run artifacts and trigger cleanup (remove temporary clusters)
customer_acceptance_matrix: Interactive-Chat / Small model: steady-state 1h, expected >= contracted_tps, p99 < 300ms -> pass/fail
Batch-Embeddings / Large model: steady-state 30m, expected tokens/sec >= contracted, p95 < 2s, error_rate < 0.1% -> pass/fail
Mixed-MultiTenant: 45m run with tenant skew, autoscaling exercise with 2x short spike -> verify scale-up and fallbacks -> pass/fail
decisions: Use k6 + custom Go prober rather than Locust to reduce Python dependency on runtime nodes
Adopt repeatable run-id naming and artifact retention of 90 days for reproducibility and audits
Require one replayed customer-run (anonymized) for any customer acceptance signoff to validate real traffic shapes
